title: A reflective subcategory of a complete category is complete
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be ordinary categories [def-nagata-category] with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. Suppose $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ is fully faithful, meaning that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(X,Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(RX,RY)$ is bijective for every $X,Y$. Suppose $R$ admits a left adjoint $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, meaning there are bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(LA,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(A,RB)$ natural in $A\in\mathcal C$ and $B\in\mathcal D$. If $\mathcal C$ is complete, then $\mathcal D$ is complete. Here a category $\mathcal E$ is complete if every $\mathcal U$-small diagram $F:J\to\mathcal E$ has a limiting cone, an object with compatible arrows to $F(j)$ through which every other cone factors uniquely.
